description: A Sallen-Key filter with a saturating feedback path, offering a lowpass or a bandpass, running sixteen polyphonic channels

params.text: Sets the cutoff, with the dial's travel raised to the fourth power so most of the fine control falls at the low end
Sets the resonance, feeding as much as four times the second pole's output into the filter's feedback term
Drives the signal into the filter as the fourth power of the dial; from the halfway point upward the output is scaled back to hold the level steady
Chooses where the signal enters the filter: LP feeds the lowpass input, BP feeds the bandpass input
Scales what the FM input does to the cutoff, from fully inverted through nothing to fully positive; the dial's travel is cubed
Scales what the V/OCT input does to the cutoff, from fully inverted through nothing to fully positive; the dial's travel is cubed

inputs.text: Adds a tenth of its voltage to the cutoff, scaled by its attenuverter, despite the tooltip on this jack reading Filter
Multiplies the cutoff by two raised to its voltage, an octave per volt with its attenuverter fully positive
The signal into the filter; the number of channels patched here is the number of channels the module runs

outputs.text: The filtered signal, one channel for each channel patched into IN

notes: the internal cutoff rate is clamped at zero, so a negative voltage at FM large enough to drive it there closes the filter
bypassing the module passes IN straight through to OUT
menu: Oversampling: off — runs the filter core once per sample and skips the decimation filter
Oversampling: x2 — runs the filter core twice per sample and decimates; the setting a new module starts with
Oversampling: x4 — runs the filter core four times per sample and decimates
Oversampling: x8 — runs the filter core eight times per sample and decimates
Decimator order: 8 — gives the Butterworth decimation filter eight poles
Decimator order: 16 — gives the Butterworth decimation filter sixteen poles; the setting a new module starts with
Decimator order: 32 — gives the Butterworth decimation filter thirty-two poles
Trapezoidal — integrates the filter state with a trapezoidal step, and is the only choice offered under the Integration Method heading
